newsitem.title: USA: Vishay to buy 65 percent of Taiwan diode maker.
newsitem.headline: Vishay to buy 65 percent of Taiwan diode maker.

text.p: Vishay Intertechnology Inc. said Friday it agreed to buy a 65 percent stake in Lite-On Power Semiconductor Corp. of Taiwan for $130 million.
Lite-On, part of Lite-On Group of China, makes diodes, semiconductor components used to convert alternating electrical currents to direct currents.
The products are used in computers, telecommunications, automotive, industrial and consumer goods.
The deal, which includes the purchase of 1.6 million warrants exercisable at $23 per share, is expected to close in mid-summer, it said.
"Vishay intends to further penetrate this market through continued acquisitions and internal growth," it said, adding that it planned to expand in Europe and Asia.
Vishay, based in Malvern, Pa., makes passive electronic components.
Its stock fell 25 cents to $22.75 early on the New York Stock Exchange.
